reasons: Lake record is verified and identifies the case as United States v. Payner, U.S. Supreme Court, year 1980.
Lake citations list official cite 447 U.S. 727, parallel cites 100 S. Ct. 2439 and 65 L. Ed. 2d 468, and vendor-neutral cite 1980 U.S. LEXIS 136.

The opinion states: "We conclude that the supervisory power does not authorize a federal court to suppress otherwise admissible evidence on the ground that it was seized unlawfully from a third party not before the court."

The opinion also states that Payner lacked Fourth Amendment standing because the search did not invade his own rights, and that accepting the supervisory-power theory would let courts disregard controlling limits.

The opinion expressly frames the doctrine as "standing to invoke the [Fourth Amendment] exclusionary rule" and applies that doctrine to reject suppression by a defendant whose own rights were not violated.
The case is a Supreme Court application of Rakas/Alderman standing principles to supervisory-power suppression, supporting placement on Standing to Challenge a Search as a key progeny case.
residual_risks: The precise curation label "Key" is not separately defined in the disclosed files, but the opinion and lake record support the role at the asserted level.
